messages:
elaine: Heads up — during the 00:00-01:00 UTC window we saw a sharp p99/p999 latency spike on the runtime fleet and KV prefix hit-rate collapsed from ~88% to ~6% for a subset of tenants. graphs: https://graf.redwood/xyZ :eyes:
paul: omg. Any recent deploys or config changes around midnight?
raj: nothing in code deploys. infra shows a cron job ran at 00:05 that does shard metadata compaction. maybe related.
toni: perf-bot flagged increased tail RPC retries and client-side backpressure.
elaine: here's the KV hit-rate panel: 
```
Tenant A: 88% -> 5% at 00:06
Tenant B: 85% -> 7% at 00:07
Global eviction rate jumped x20
```
paul: looking at ops history — we enabled a new compaction mode two nights ago: `compact --affinity=rebalance --reset-prefix-ttl` scheduled at 00:05 daily. I didn't think reset-prefix-ttl would touch live routing.
raj: "reset-prefix-ttl" sounds deadly for hot prefixes. That would remove TTL gating and force immediate eviction of cached KV prefixes. Could cause cold starts and cascading miss amplification.
elaine: confirmed. `/var/log/compactor/2026-03-14.log` shows the command executed and returned 0. excerpt:
```
[00:05:12] compactor: starting round
[00:05:13] compactor: rebalancing shards
[00:05:14] compactor: reset-prefix-ttl applied to 42k prefixes
[00:05:14] compactor: finished
```
logan: customer hit error budgets, pinged us — they saw a 6x increase in latency on their inference route.
toni: can we roll back the compaction flag? Paul — can you disable cron and trigger a focused reconciliation to restore prefix TTLs?
paul: disabling cron now. I'll also run a TTL restore job that rehydrates top prefixes from warm snapshots.
paul: running: `compactor --restore-prefix-ttl --from=snapshot-20260313 --filter=top-50k`
raj: profiling data during spike shows kernel selection fell back to generic GEMM for many short sequences because batch sampler changed distribution. Batch acceptance dropped from 180->40 per cycle. CPU time per token spiked. snippet from perf:
```
kernel_choice: fallback_generic (80%)
batch_size_median: 18 -> 6
latency_token_ms_p99: 120 -> 920
```
elaine: so two orthogonal things: compaction reset TTLs -> eviction flood; AND sampler/batching heuristics responded to the miss stream and started creating smaller batches that triggered a less-optimized kernel path.
toni: that's a noisy-neighbor amplification effect. eviction -> hotter load on model -> smaller batches -> worse kernel -> higher latency -> more eviction pressure.
paul: TTL-restore job completed, rehydrated ~37k prefixes. I'm re-enabling read-through caching and bumping warm cache allocation for affected shards.
paul: patch pushed to compactor: default no-op for `--reset-prefix-ttl` unless `--force=explicit`, and cron removed from daily schedule.
raj: also changed batching sampler to keep a small buffer threshold so it doesn't collapse to tiny batches on transient miss bursts. config: `batcher.min_accept=40` (was 8).
elaine: after fixes, metrics are recovering: p99 back to baseline within ~7 minutes of restore. KV hit-rate climbed back to 75% -> 82% over 12m.
perf-bot: Incident annotated: root cause = compactor flag reset-prefix-ttl combined with batcher sensitivity to miss storms. Recommendations: (1) remove dangerous default flags, (2) add guardrail alert for mass-prefix-ttl-reset, (3) tune batcher.min_accept and profile hot-kernel fallback thresholds.
logan: relayed to customer, they accepted the post-mortem summary.
toni: action items assigned: Paul->compactor safe defaults + cron removal, Raj->batcher guard, Elaine->postmortem writeup + SPoF avoidance checklist.
elaine: thanks all. tagging followup for next oncall to watch for similar eviction waves. :white_check_mark:
